we propose a new framework to learn optimal filters from the data for extracting dynamical system features from EEG signals, and that these features are competitive with the CSP features and the AR features for the classification of EEG signals.

(i) the dynamical system features outperform the CSP features in the EEG classification problem, (ii) the Fisher ratio criterion is an effective approach to optimize spatial filters for EEG classification, and (iii) the temporal filters learned using Fisher ratio criterion can further improve the performance.
we propose to use features from dynamical system theory to classify motor-imagery EEG, and we propose to use Fisher ratio criterion to automatically learn optimal filters from the data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and the evaluation of a new approach to the classification of EEG signals for brain-computer interface.
the development of a new feature set and the learning of optimal spatial and temporal filters for EEG classification in the context of BCI.

the following: 1) the use of dynamical system features for EEG classification; 2) the development of an automatic learning framework for learning optimal spatial and temporal filters; and 3) a comparative study of the proposed features with the CSP features, which have been used extensively in the past for EEG classification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed dynamical features and the learning framework provide a competitive alternative to the CSP and the other state of the art approaches for EEG based BCIs.

the proposed dynamical features, along with the spatial and temporal filters learned using the proposed approach, are a very competitive option in terms of classification accuracy and generalization capability, and are a very good alternative to the CSP and the autoregressive features.
the proposed features and the learning framework for optimal spatial and temporal filters provide a competitive alternative for EEG-based BCI applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a framework that learns optimal filters from the data, and then uses the learned filters to extract novel features for classification.

we propose a novel framework for learning optimal spatial and temporal filters for dynamical system features from multichannel EEG data for classification, and demonstrate the competitive performance of the features with the CSP, the AR features and the conventional spatial filters.

we have developed a novel framework for feature learning from multivariate time-series data, and have shown that it can yield competitive results when used for classification of EEG signals for BCI applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dynamical system features, which are extracted directly from the raw EEG signals, are competitive with other popular EEG features.
the proposed dynamical features can be used as a complementary set of features for BCI applications.
dynamical system features and the proposed filter learning framework are promising for BCI classification, which can be further exploited for other EEG-based applications.
